understanding.emotion: I have decided, and I am ready to begin
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call starting what is yours to build, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.insight: You have decided, and the decision is your own. The hard part comes on the morning the work stops being exciting.
understanding.mechanism_label: Starting what is yours to build

I want to change careers but I'm scared
I can't tell if continuing is discipline or stubbornness

queries.hook: A fire lit by seeing what others achieved; the resolve to rise, gather your strength and take on what is yours to do.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.
queries.story: A story of someone who set out to build or win something that was theirs to do, met the first test, and kept going.

understanding.life_context: Working and building something of their own and raising kids. Feels determined; closest to "I can't control my cravings" and "I want to reconnect with my roots".

plan_v3.first_line: Your hope for Vrindavan meets the gnawing fear of withdrawal, yet you still hold your intention to heal.

hook.speaker: Nidagha
hook.sanskrit: यां यामहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ संश्रयामि गुणश्रियम् । तां तां कृन्तति मे तृष्णा तन्त्रीमिव कुमूषिका ॥
hook.line: Every good quality I take up, craving gnaws through, like a mouse chewing a string.
hook.translation: Whatever good quality I take refuge in, great sage, craving cuts it away, as a mouse gnaws through a string.
hook.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.
